Architectural Craft

Built for people who trust verifiable pipelines.

Every view—Table Mode, Canvas DAG, Code Preview, CLI, and MCP—operates on a single deterministic workflow.json v1.0 contract.

01 / ENGINE

Native CSV, Excel (.xlsx) & Parquet

Zero-dependency multi-sheet .xlsx reader/writer verified round-trip with openpyxl, streaming RFC 4180 CSV parser, CSV Formula Injection Guard, and pluggable DuckDbWasmAdapter for Parquet.

02 / DATA TRUST

Contracts, Schema Drift & Regression

Auto-generate JSON Schema 2020-12 snapshots, catch Critical/High breaking changes before PR merge, enforce Data Contracts, and run automated Workflow Regression Tests in GitHub Actions.

03 / CLEANING

OpenRefine-Style Fuzzy Clustering

Merge messy categorical variants ("New-York", "new york ", "Enterprize") using Key-Collision Fingerprints and Levenshtein edit distance—zero Java install required.

04 / PRIVACY

PII Sentinel & Zero-Data Recipes

Detect emails, phones, tokens, and IDs locally; apply Mask, Hash, Synthetic, or Keep-Last-N redaction; share workflow recipes via URL hash without ever embedding customer rows.

05 / AI-NATIVE API

10-Tool MCP & OpenAPI 3.1 REST

Built for Claude, Gemini, and Cursor: fuzzy node aliases, Levenshtein didYouMean error recovery, automatic PII masking on previews, token-budget compact mode, and localhost OpenAPI.

06 / CANVAS & GRID

Multi-Port DAG & Virtualized Grid

Wire out and errors branches visually across nodes, scroll smoothly through 10k+ rows in constant ~45 DOM rows, and edit node parameters with column dropdowns instead of raw JSON.

The Craft Behind The Tool

Why Monday-morning data cleanup deserved better.

Every operations lead, analyst, and backend engineer knows the quiet dread of a recurring export. A supplier sends an updated 40,000-row Excel catalog where column order shifted. A Stripe or Shopify CSV arrives with mixed 02/03/2026 and ISO dates, duplicate order IDs from retried webhooks, stray semicolons, and customer emails in three different cases.

Historically, you had three bad choices: paste sensitive customer PII into an ad-supported online converter, wrestle with fragile Excel VLOOKUP formulas that silently strip leading zeros and execute =HYPERLINK payloads, or spend half an hour rewriting a one-off Python script no one on the team can inspect visually.

Data Workbench 2.4 was built to end that trade-off. Everything runs locally inside your browser Web Worker with zero uploads—and every click in Table Mode or Canvas Mode compiles into one deterministic workflow.json you can version in Git, run in your terminal via dw, enforce in GitHub Actions, or expose safely to Claude, Cursor, and Gemini over MCP.

“Good data tools shouldn’t force you to choose between visual clarity, local privacy, and CI-grade repeatability.”

Questions & Trust

Clear answers before you drop a file.

Does Data Workbench upload my CSV, Excel, or JSON files to a server?

Never. All parsing, Data Quality Radar profiling, fuzzy clustering, primary-key diffing, and exports run locally inside your browser Web Worker or local Node.js CLI. Zero cell values or filenames leave your machine.

How fast is Data Workbench on 100,000-row spreadsheets?

Powered by a zero-dependency Selection-Vector columnar engine (TypedArrays + dictionary predicate pushdown), Data Workbench imports 100,000 × 25 CSV rows (12.74 MB) in 711 ms, filters in 8.7 ms, and deduplicates in 26.5 ms using ~25.1 MB of estimated RAM.

Does it support Excel (.xlsx) and protect against CSV/Excel formula injection?

Yes. Data Workbench ships a zero-dependency multi-sheet .xlsx reader and writer verified bidirectionally with Python openpyxl, and enables Formula Injection Protection by default—safely escaping cells starting with =, +, -, or @.

How can I connect Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to Data Workbench?

Launch the sandboxed MCP server with npx data-workbench-mcp --sandbox ./data to expose 10 deterministic tools (with fuzzy node aliases, didYouMean typo recovery, and automatic PII redaction), or run npm run api for a localhost-only OpenAPI 3.1 REST server.
